papers.title: Dream-Tac: A Unified Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Yunfan Lou, Yifan Ye, Yankai Fu, Jun Cen, Xiaowei Chi, Yaoxu Lyu, Peidong Jia, Sirui Han
papers.abstract: World action models inherit the predictive capability of world models, enabling action generation to be guided by anticipated future observations. However, they rely primarily on vision and often fail in contact-rich manipulation, where critical cues arise from physical interaction. In this paper, we propose Dream-Tac, a unified Tactile-World Action Model that jointly models actions, future visual observations, and tactile dynamics. Specifically, Dream-Tac introduces (i) contact-gated visuotactile fusion to selectively integrate tactile signals and (ii) a contact-aware attention bias to better regulate cross-modal interactions during manipulation. To support real-time deployment, we further design a dual-level acceleration strategy, reformulating the contact-aware bias to preserve the fused attention path during training and introducing cache-based diffusion acceleration at inference, achieving up to 2.9$\times$ faster training and 1.8$\times$ faster inference. Across six contact-rich manipulation tasks, Dream-Tac improves action accuracy by 31.7\% on average, demonstrating the effectiveness of unified visuotactile world modeling.Code is available at https://github.com/LYFCLOUDFAN/Dream-Tac.

papers.title: Doc2DT: An LLM-driven knowledge graph abstraction framework for digital twin generation from unstructured engineering documents
papers.authors: Yongho Lee, Sol Choi, Sang Won Lee
papers.abstract: Engineering documents contain substantial knowledge about the structure, behavior, and operation of physical systems, yet this knowledge is typically expressed in heterogeneous human-readable forms that are difficult to directly reuse in computational engineering workflows. As a result, the development of digital twins often relies on domain-specific modeling procedures and extensive manual engineering effort, limiting the reuse of generation methodologies across different systems. To address this challenge, this paper proposes Doc2DT, an LLM-driven knowledge graph abstraction framework that transforms unstructured engineering documents into reusable digital twin representations through a unified abstraction process. The framework converts document-level engineering information into structured digital representations and reformulates them as graph-based abstract models that explicitly capture engineering knowledge in a machine-interpretable form. The resulting abstraction serves as the foundation for digital twin generation and system integration. The proposed framework is evaluated through industrial robot case studies in which engineering documents are transformed into validated digital representations and deployed as operational digital twins. Additional robot casesfurther demonstrate that the same abstraction methodology can be retained despite differences in geometry, document structure, and local ambiguity. The results support the effectiveness, generality, and scalability of the proposed abstraction-centered approach within the articulated robot domain and indicate a broader pathway toward reusable digital twin generation from heterogeneous engineering documents.

papers.title: DobotTrack: Target-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Learning for Embodied Person Tracking
papers.authors: Shengjun Deng, Yinghan Zhang, Chengrui Wei, Liu Liang, Songyuan Liu, Pengkun Zheng, Yajun Zheng, Ying Zhang, et al.
papers.abstract: Language-guided embodied person tracking requires a mobile agent to identify a target from a referring description and consistently follow the target under egocentric observations. We present DobotTrack, a target-grounded vision-language-action (VLA) framework that integrates auxiliary grounding supervision with efficient temporal modeling. We systematically investigate five auxiliary tasks---person segmentation, bounding-box grounding, visual-spatial classification (VSC), future DINO feature prediction, and future-frame prediction---and adopt complementary mask and bounding-box supervision to enhance target delineation and localization. We introduce Q-identity, a target-conditioned historical visual compression module that leverages target-grounding predictions to selectively preserve identity-discriminative appearance features and spatial cues in compact historical tokens. On EVT-Bench, our 0.8B-parameter model achieves an average success rate of 77.9%, exceeding OmTrackVLA by 16.9 percentage points across the three tasks. We further construct a real-world person-tracking dataset collected using a quadruped robot, comprising 126 episodes and 596,323 mask-annotated frames. The target masks enable automatic derivation of bounding boxes and visual-spatial labels encoding horizontal position and apparent image scale, providing additional grounding supervision without separate manual annotation of these labels. Together, our framework and annotation pipeline support learning target-grounded tracking policies from simulated and real-world data. Code is available at https://github.com/Dobot-Team/dobot_track.

papers.title: DexDICE: Reconciling Safety and Performance via Dual-Expert Offline Imitation Learning
papers.authors: Seokin Seo, Sung Kuk Shyn, Minji Seo, Yisoo Lee, Jongmin Lee, Hongseok Yang, Kee-Eung Kim
papers.abstract: Ensuring high returns while providing strong safety guarantees in offline imitation learning (IL) is a fundamental challenge: existing approaches either rely on explicitly specified cost functions, which are difficult to design for complex real-world safety constraints, or require expert demonstrations that are both safe and high-performing, which are often too costly to collect. We introduce dual-expert imitation learning, which leverages two complementary data sources: (i) safety-compliant demonstrations that faithfully follow safety guidelines but may be suboptimal, and (ii) performance-oriented demonstrations that achieve high returns but may violate safety guidelines. To address this problem, we propose DexDICE (Dual-expert offline imitation learning via stationary DIstribution Correction Estimation). Instead of conventional distribution constraints, DexDICE combines DICE-style offline learning with safe support constraints, enabling agents to exploit high-return behaviors while remaining within safety-compliant regions. We prove that the ideal solution satisfying this constraint exactly has zero unsafe-region visitation with high probability. We evaluate DexDICE on a re-curated DSRL benchmark and validate it on a real-world mobile-robot navigation task trained directly from human teleoperation demonstrations, where it substantially outperforms baselines and remains robust to data scarcity and quality degradation.

papers.title: Deep learning–based object detection for automated classification of ripe and unripe tomatoes in field conditions
papers.authors: Leila Hassanzadeh, Razieh Pourdarbani, Sajad Sabzi, Omid Daliran, José Miguel Molina‐Martínez, Ginés Garcı́a-Mateos, Alberto García-Berná
papers.abstract: Accurate detection of tomatoes at different ripening stages from close-range remote sensing imagery acquired under real field conditions is a key enabler for yield estimation, harvest scheduling, and selective robotic picking in precision agriculture. However, achieving reliable performance is challenging due to occlusions, variable illumination, dense foliage, and the limited size of domain-specific datasets typically available to small farms and research teams. In this work, we present a controlled comparative study between two representative object detection paradigms, Faster R-CNN with a ResNet-50 FPN backbone (two-stage) and YOLO26s (single-stage), on a curated dataset of 367 high-resolution images acquired in a commercial cherry-tomato greenhouse under natural illumination, containing more than 8,900 manually annotated tomatoes across three classes: blossom, premature, and ripe. Both models were trained for 100 epochs under a controlled protocol sharing the same data, stratified 70/15/15 split complemented by 5-fold cross-validation, and evaluated using COCO-style AP/AR together with per-class precision–recall and ROC analyses. YOLO26s achieved a macro-average AP of 0.741 and ROC AUC of 0.954 on the held-out test split, substantially outperforming Faster R-CNN (macro AP 0.241; ROC AUC 0.836), particularly under stricter localization thresholds, and qualitative examples confirm that localization rather than classification is the main bottleneck of Faster R-CNN. These results provide actionable guidelines for deploying detectors on small agricultural remote sensing datasets in fixed monitoring stations and on ground or aerial autonomous platforms, where tighter bounding boxes and a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off are decisive for reliable operation.

papers.title: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Dingkun Wei, Zehong Shen, Huaijin Pi, Xueyang Wang, Xing Zhu, Hujun Bao, Yujun Shen, Xiaowei Zhou
papers.abstract: Humanoid whole-body control requires a robot to track diverse reference motions while maintaining balance under gravity, torque limits, contact switching, and external disturbances. Existing reinforcement-learning-based trackers typically learn control outputs that jointly address motion tracking and balance. However, similar reference poses can correspond to substantially different dynamic demands, requiring a unified policy to learn motion-dependent control requirements alongside balance corrections. This can complicate learning and lead to high-frequency fluctuations in control outputs. We propose DKWBC, a dynamics-informed whole-body control framework that combines explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual. Inspired by the model-based and environmental-wrench contributions to joint torques in floating-base dynamics, DKWBC uses inverse-dynamics feedforward and joint PD feedback to supply tracking torques, while a residual policy learns additional joint-torque corrections for balanced execution. By explicitly accounting for motion-dependent torque demands, this structure simplifies the policy's learning task. Experiments in simulation and on real hardware demonstrate that a single learned balancing policy generalizes across motion datasets while maintaining accurate motion tracking and balance across ground support, attached payloads, and physical interaction. papers.title: Continuous Versus Discrete Tactile Representations for Vision-Language-Action Avocado Sorting
papers.authors: Ran Yang, Yuhao Lei, Li Yang, Yiming Feng
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies typically have no direct channel for non-visual physical properties, such as tactile ripeness: such evidence is either dropped entirely or folded into the policy as a discrete signal, a classifier output substituted into a text prompt. The latter reuses the language channel VLA models are pretrained on, but compresses a spatially structured deformation field into a low-bandwidth categorical cue represented by only a few language tokens. We investigate how the pathway used to incorporate tactile evidence affects contact-rich manipulation. Using robotic avocado ripeness sorting as a testbed, where tactile deformation cues are inaccessible to vision, we compare three conditions: a vision-only pi0 baseline with no tactile signal, discrete text-prompt conditioning on a separately trained tactile classifier, and continuous fusion, where GelSight tactile images are encoded via a pretrained DINOv2 encoder and concatenated with visual embeddings prior to the pi0 backbone, without added cross-modal attention. In a small-scale evaluation on 10 held-out avocados unseen during demonstration collection, with each specimen tested twice per method, continuous fusion reaches a 95% sorting success rate, versus 80% for discrete text-prompt conditioning and 70% with no tactile signal, at only 7.7% inference overhead over the vision-only baseline; the discrete classifier matches the specimen label in all 20 of its robot trials. The central observation is that even a correct tactile category can fail to control a pretrained action policy when communicated only through a prompt.

papers.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
papers.authors: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck
papers.abstract: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning. These results suggest that the skills CUAs learn on software, such as visual grounding, precise clicking, and exploration, already carry over to embodied tasks, giving CUAs a far broader scope in embodied AI than previously realized. We therefore advocate that computer-use agents can be embodied generalists. Further, we advocate that, by following the training strategy that made computer-use agents general, embodied AI can converge on a single general model as well, ushering in a new era of general embodied AI. papers.title: CoT4AD: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Explicit Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Zhaohui Wang, Tengbo Yu, Hao Tang
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently attracted growing attention in end-to-end autonomous driving for their strong reasoning capabilities and rich world knowledge. However, existing VLAs often suffer from limited numerical reasoning ability and overly simplified input-output mappings, which hinder their performance in complex driving scenarios requiring step-by-step causal reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose CoT4AD, a novel VLA framework that introduces Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning for autonomous driving to enhance both numerical and causal reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs). CoT4AD integrates visual observations and language instructions to perform semantic reasoning, scene understanding, and trajectory planning. During training, it explicitly models a perception-question-prediction-action CoT to align the reasoning space with the action space across multiple driving tasks. During inference, it performs implicit CoT reasoning to enable consistent numerical reasoning and robust decision-making in dynamic environments. Extensive experiments on both real-world and simulated benchmarks, including nuScenes and Bench2Drive, demonstrate that CoT4AD achieves state-of-the-art performance in both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations. papers.title: Capturability-Aware Footstep Planning in Cluttered Environments: A Recursively Feasible Sequential MPC on Axis-Aligned Safe Corridors
papers.authors: Athanasios Kyriakopoulos, Shubham S. Kumbhar, Kunal S. Narkhede, Abhijeet M. Kulkarni, Ioannis Poulakakis
papers.abstract: A fundamental aspect of humanoid footstep planning is to jointly guarantee obstacle avoidance and locomotion stability. This paper presents a capturability-aware sequential Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for Linear Inverted Pendulum (LIP)-based humanoid footstep planning in the presence of obstacles. The proposed method combines obstacle avoidance with capturability constraints through safe corridors constructed as sequences of intersecting rectangles, yielding a sequential MPC framework with recursive feasibility guarantees for the LIP-based planning layer. The planner autonomously adapts to constrained scenarios, switching to in-place walking when obstructions---such as doors assumed to be open during planning but unexpectedly found to be closed during execution---block forward motion. Performance is largely independent of the prediction horizon, allowing high success rates while keeping the computational cost low. The approach is validated in high-fidelity simulations with the humanoid robot Digit, demonstrating a practical solution for capturable humanoid footstep planning in cluttered environments.

papers.title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
papers.authors: Jusheng Zhang, Keze Wang, Liang Lin
papers.abstract: A language model can repair a robot policy's lexical instruction grounding by editing just 65 token-embedding rows. We bring weight-space programming to robot foundation policies: GPT-6 Astra reads weights and uses a CPU workspace and budgeted simulator feedback, without gradient updates or new demonstrations. Three independent sessions on $π_{0.5}$ all improve success on 765 held-out paraphrases; the best raises success from 86.3\% to 92.0\% (48 repairs, four regressions; exact paired $p=1.31\times10^{-10}$). Among the 335 instructions containing edited tokens, success rises from 74.3\% to 87.5\%; the other 430 episodes have zero outcome changes. Matched random-direction edits do not help. Full replacement using the editor's own lexicon explains much of the gain but produces more regressions; its direct difference from the editor is not significant at 0.05. Across 13 further robot sessions, the editor declines 12 candidates; the sole retained edit does not show a significant held-out gain. Separately, benchmark metadata lowers FastWAM success from 70.0\% to 48.6\%, while the evaluated VLA's aggregate rate is unchanged. The evidence supports precise lexical repair, not general acquisition of missing robot capabilities.

papers.title: CARA: Concept-Aware Risk Attention for Interpretable Collision Anticipation
papers.authors: Zhishan Tao, Ruoyu Wang, Yucheng Wu, Enjun Du, Yilei Yuan, Sherwin Ho, Y W Su, Jinbo Su
papers.abstract: Collision anticipation in autonomous driving requires not only accurate early warnings but also interpretable reasoning about what risk factors are being tracked and how risk evolves over time. Existing methods fall short in this regard: feature-driven models are opaque, post-hoc explanations often lack fidelity, and concept-based methods are mostly designed for static recognition rather than dynamic driving scenes. We propose CARA (Concept-Aware Risk Attention), an intrinsically interpretable spatio-temporal framework for collision anticipation. CARA derives domain-grounded risk concepts from accident narratives, aligns them with video frames via vision-language similarity, and organizes them into evolving concept trajectories. These trajectories provide explicit risk evidence that guides spatial attention, temporal attention, and anticipation, allowing semantic concepts to directly influence both where the model attends and how it predicts risk over time. By treating semantic risk factors as dynamic intermediate evidence rather than auxiliary post-hoc explanations, CARA tightly couples interpretability with the predictive process. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show that CARA consistently improves anticipation accuracy and warning earliness over strong baselines, while providing sparse and semantically grounded concept evidence.

papers.title: Bioprinted aquatic plant-inspired soft machines for underwater environmental sensing
papers.authors: Isabella Fiorello, Israel Kellersztein, Beatriz Arsuffi, Frederike Klimm, Barbara Mazzolai, Thomas Speck, Chiara Daraio
papers.abstract: Abstract Aquatic plants combine porous, compliant stems with distributed leaves that interact with complex underwater environments, but these design principles remain unexplored in soft robotics. Here we translate the architecture and biomechanics of the submerged macrophyte Myriophyllum mattogrossense into bioprinted aquatic plant-inspired soft machines. High-resolution photon-based bioprinting produced wheel-like porous hydrogel stems with approximately 38% lower flexural rigidity than solid controls (15.6±2.1 versus 25.1±2.8 N mm²), enabling large deformations under external loading. We fabricated leaf-like structures using two cellulose-based hydrogel systems. Sodium alginate-hydroxyethyl cellulose hydrogels containing Chlamydomonas reinhardtii showed progressive greening and chlorophyll autofluorescence during culture. Nanocellulose-based poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) hydrogels underwent reversible shape changes in response to temperature and salinity, with curvature increasing 6.5-fold and 4-fold, respectively. Integrating these components produced an artificial aquatic plant-like machine that remained stable underwater while retaining the mechanical and responsive properties of its stem and leaf modules. These results establish aquatic plant architecture as a source of design principles for modular biohybrid soft machines and provide a foundation for underwater environmental sensing. This responsive platform offers a route towards adaptive underwater devices for environmental monitoring, ecological research and future biohybrid robotic applications across diverse, dynamic aquatic ecosystems.

papers.title: Beyond Waypoints: A Trajectory-Centric Waypointing Paradigm for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.authors: Haoxiang Shi, Xiang Deng, Haoyu Zhang, Qiaohui Chu, Yaowei Wang, Liqiang Nie
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires agents to follow natural-language instructions while navigating in real-world-like environments. Most VLN-CE approach\-es adopt a three-stage framework: a waypoint predictor proposes navigable waypoints, and a navigator selects the best waypoint, with a low-level controller executing the movement to it. However, this decoupled paradigm often leads to unreachable waypoints or inconsistencies between planning and control. In this work, instead of predicting isolated waypoints, we introduce a novel paradigm called Trajectory Waypoint, which grounds each candidate waypoint in an executable trajectory. To realize this, we design a Trajectory Waypoint Predictor formulated as a TSDF-guided diffusion policy, which steers trajectory generation away from obstacles, inherently ensuring the reachability of the predicted waypoints. We further propose a trajectory-enhanced navigator that injects the associated trajectory as additional information for planning, enabling strict consistency between high-level semantic decisions and low-level execution. Extensive experiments on the VLN-CE benchmark show that our Trajectory Waypoint paradigm achieves superior performance over the baselines.

papers.title: Beyond Frame-Level Accuracy: Analyzing Video-Level Stability in Transformer-Based Deepfake Forensics
papers.authors: Syed Azmul Hasan, Mowmita Pervin Hera, Afroza Lona Mim, M M Jihad Hossain, Hazrat Ali, Mohammad Farhad Bulbul
papers.abstract: Deepfake videos generated by advanced generative models pose serious threats to digital security, misinformation control, and media forensics. Although numerous detection methods have been proposed, their reported performances are often based on heterogeneous preprocessing pipelines, inconsistent data splits, and model-specific training protocols, hindering fair architectural comparison. This work presents a controlled and reproducible comparative study of convolutional neural networks (ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0) and a transformer-based architecture (ViT-B/16) within a unified, face-centric deepfake detection framework. All models are trained using identical preprocessing, augmentation, optimization settings, and data splits on Celeb-DF v2 and FaceForensics++, and results are validated across three independent random seeds with bootstrapped confidence intervals. Experimental results show that while CNN-based models perform competitively at the frame level, their performance degrades after video-level aggregation. In contrast, ViT-B/16 demonstrates more stable video-level performance, achieving 92.8\% [95\% CI: 91.7--94.0] video-level accuracy and an AUC of 0.950 [95\% CI: 0.934--0.964] on Celeb-DF v2 (3-seed bootstrapped). Cross-dataset evaluation across the same three random seeds reveals a large, asymmetric generalization gap (AUC 0.79 FF++$\rightarrow$Celeb-DF vs. 0.64 Celeb-DF$\rightarrow$FF++), indicating that in-domain video-level stability does not transfer to unseen manipulation domains. These findings indicate that global self-attention improves robustness and video-level stability for deepfake detection within a given data domain, while highlighting the need for further work on cross-domain generalization.

papers.abstract: Human demonstrations provide a scalable source of diverse manipulation data, but leveraging them for robot learning remains challenging due to differences in embodiment, viewpoint, action spaces, and temporal structure. BATCH learns self-supervised temporal representations with a cycle-consistency objective to establish cross-embodiment correspondences without manual annotation. We further introduce two complementary training objectives that leverage these correspondences within an autoregressive videoaction diffusion model: behavior-aligned co-training and human-to-robot style transfer. On real-world manipulation tasks, BATCH improves generalization to unseen task configurations compared with training on unaligned data and prior cross-embodiment baselines, with additional gains from the style-transfer objective. papers.title: Augmentron: Scalable Multi-View Visual Augmentation for Robot Learning

This produces temporally and multi-view consistent environ- ment and workspace variations while preserving the robot, task objects, actions, and annotations. The results show that introducing augmented data to a data training recipe can help policies generalize to dynamic real-world settings.

The platform integrates four-wheel independent swerve drive, swappable computing, distributed embedded control, multimodal sensing, and configurable manipulation within a unified sense-plan-act-verify framework supporting perception, control, navigation, manipulation, and autonomous task verification. These proof-of-concept tasks, controller-tuning studies, and integrated trials demonstrate the platform's research capabilities, while its accessible and reconfigurable design supports its use for hands-on robotics education. By combining affordability, modularity, open-source accessibility, configurable manipulation, and end-to-end sense-plan-act-verify autonomy, Agibot provides a practical platform for agricultural robotics research, technology development, and workforce training.

papers.title: AeroGuide: Grounded Vision-Language Navigation in Aerial Environments
papers.authors: Abhinav Upadhyay, Siddharth Singh, Satvik Srivastava, Tanya Khanna, Ashutosh Pandey, Shashi Shekhar Jha
papers.abstract: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) requires a UAV to follow natural language instructions from visual observations. Aerial VLN is more challenging than ground-level VLN because UAV observations cover large outdoor areas, landmarks often occupy only a small part of the image, and navigation requires complex spatial reasoning. General-purpose vision-language models (VLMs) often struggle to identify instruction-relevant visual evidence from such dense aerial observations. We propose AeroGuide, a grounded aerial VLN framework built on Qwen3-VL. AeroGuide introduces Navigation-conditioned Visual Token Routing (NVTR), which selects instruction-relevant visual tokens conditioned on the current observation, UAV pose, and temporal landmark memory. AeroGuide maintains an egocentric temporal landmark memory that retains compact landmark evidence rather than full historical frames. The model is trained through multiple phases, including supervised learning, reasoning distillation, and simulator-based policy optimization, to improve grounded action prediction and closed-loop navigation. On the OpenFly benchmark, AeroGuide improves navigation success rate from 34.3% to 45.1%, a 31.5% relative improvement over the best-performing prior baseline. Ablation studies show that explicit visual grounding and compact temporal memory are key contributors to this improvement, demonstrating the effectiveness of grounded navigation for aerial VLN. papers.title: Advancements in Embedded Surveillance Robotics for Defense and Security Applications
papers.authors: Ramji Gupta, Manju Yadav, Alpana Pandey
papers.abstract: In military applications, surveillance plays a critical role in ensuring security, particularly in isolated and border areas. This chapter presents a recent approach to surveillance using a robot for military applications. The planned methodology is to substitute soldiers in border areas with robots, to enhance the security and both autonomous and manual control via internet connectivity. Equipped with multiple sensors and various electronic devices, the robot is designed to detect enemy presence, capture camera footage, and live-stream data to authorized personnel. This robot enables armed forces to proficiently monitor isolated areas and respond immediately to potential threats. Human risk is reduced by using this type of robot surveillance system. Deploying robots in high-risk isolated areas minimizes personnel exposure to potential threats while maintaining effective surveillance. The use of autonomous technology increases operational efficiency by enabling continuous surveillance without requiring constant human intervention. By combining cutting-edge embedded technology, real-time monitoring, and remote operability, this robot vehicle delivers a consistent and effective solution for border or boundary security. Integrating advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), embedded systems, and very large-scale integration (VLSI), will significantly enhance the capabilities and efficiency of the robot in armed forces. This robot provides not only a human-free system but also an efficient smart system to address military challenges.

papers.title: Adaptive dual-programming magnetic soft robot with lifelike behavior
papers.authors: Yanchen Ye, Can Xu, Sen Wang, Weijia Li, Rongye Wu, Hao Wu, Neng Xia, TianYe Yang
papers.abstract: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated "locomotion-perception-action" workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.

papers.title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Sungwon Moon, Minji Kim, Hyemin Boo, Daeun Song, Jiyoung Lee
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control. Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation. We propose \ours, a training-free token pruning method that moves the pruning decision ahead of the vision encoder by grounding it in a geometric prior derived from the robot's own action. The action chunk predicted at the previous control step is already available before the current observation is encoded, and it specifies the end-effector and camera motion between consecutive observations. The same action affects the two standard camera views asymmetrically: in the fixed third-person view, \ours retains patches along the projected end-effector trajectory together with semantic anchors, while in the wrist view, it prunes patches that remain unchanged after compensating for the action-induced camera motion. Extensive experiments on two simulation environments (LIBERO and VLABench) and four real-robot tasks demonstrate that \ours achieves up to 1.61 $\times$ speedup and 59.5\% FLOPs reduction with negligible degradation in success rates.

papers.title: ActDistill: General Action-Guided Self-Derived Distillation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Wencheng Ye, Tianshi Wang, Fengling Li, Lei Zhu, Heng Tao Shen
papers.abstract: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown impressive flexibility and generalization, yet their deployment in robotic manipulation remains limited by heavy computational overhead and inference latency. In this work, we present ActDistill, a general action-guided self-derived distillation framework that transfers the action prediction capability of any existing VLA model to a lightweight counterpart. Unlike previous efficiency strategies that primarily emphasize vision-language correlations, ActDistill leverages action priors to guide knowledge transfer and model compression, achieving action-oriented efficiency for VLA models. Specifically, we employ a well-trained VLA model as the teacher and introduce a graph-structured encapsulation strategy to explicitly model the hierarchical evolution of action prediction. The student model, derived from the graph-encapsulated teacher, is further equipped with a dynamic router that adaptively selects computation paths based on action prediction demands, guided by hierarchical graph-informed supervision to ensure smooth and efficient evolution. During inference, graph-related auxiliary components are removed, allowing the student to execute only dynamically routed layers and predict high-precision actions with minimal computation and latency. Experiments on embodied benchmarks demonstrate that ActDistill achieves comparable or superior performance to full-scale VLA models while reducing computation by over 50% with up to 1.67 times speedup, thereby establishing a general paradigm toward efficient embodied intelligence.

papers.title: ATLAS: A Multi-Procedure Benchmark and Context-Aware Model for Surgical Anatomy Segmentation
papers.authors: Ronald L. P. D. de Jong, Tim J. M. Jaspers, Raf A. H. Vervoort, Aron F. H. A. Bakker, Anna L. Dijk, Yiping Li, Jip L. Tolenaar, Jelle P. Ruurda, et al.
papers.abstract: Recognizing anatomical structures during minimally invasive surgery (MIS) could support intraoperative navigation and improve patient safety, but progress is limited by small, single-procedure datasets and by segmentation methods developed for natural scenes. This work addresses both limitations through a new dataset and model. First, we introduce ATLAS-120k, a clip-level semantic segmentation dataset of 121,018 annotated frames from 100 surgical videos, covering 14 laparoscopic and robot-assisted procedures and 41 classes. Annotations were created with a pipeline that combines manual labeling, tracker-based propagation, and review by surgeons. Second, we propose ATLAS (Anatomy Recognition with Context Learning using Foundation Representations), a video semantic segmentation model for surgical anatomy recognition. ATLAS builds on in-domain foundation-model embeddings and adds context queries for the procedure and surgical phase, together with query propagation between frames for short-term memory. ATLAS outperforms state-of-the-art natural-image and in-domain foundation models in both segmentation accuracy and temporal consistency, achieving a Dice score of 0.70 with ViT-L while running in real time at 76.2 FPS. Ablations show that the context queries improve accuracy and that query propagation improves temporal consistency. ATLAS also generalizes well, matching a dedicated model zero-shot on CholecSeg8k and improving phase recognition on AutoLaparo over SurgeNet initialization. The model weights, dataset annotations, and annotation tool are publicly available at https://github.com/TimJaspers0801/ATLAS.

papers.title: ARFlow: Real-time Human Action-Reaction Synthesis with Reprojection Guidance
papers.authors: Wentao Jiang, Jingya Wang, Kaiyang Ji, Baoxiong Jia, Siyuan Huang, Ye Shi
papers.abstract: Human action-reaction synthesis, a fundamental challenge in modeling causal human interactions, plays a critical role in applications ranging from virtual reality to social robotics. While diffusion-based models have demonstrated promising performance, they exhibit two key limitations for interaction synthesis: reliance on complex noise-to-reaction generators with intricate conditional mechanisms, and frequent physical violations in generated motions. To address these issues, we propose Action-Reaction Flow Matching (ARFlow), a novel framework that establishes direct action-to-reaction mappings, eliminating the need for complex conditional mechanisms. Our approach introduces a physical guidance mechanism specifically designed for Flow Matching (FM) that effectively prevents body penetration artifacts during sampling. Moreover, we discover the bias of traditional flow matching sampling algorithm and employ a reprojection method to revise the sampling direction of FM. To further enhance the reaction diversity, we incorporate randomness into the sampling process. Extensive experiments on NTU120, Chi3D and InterHuman datasets demonstrate that ARFlow not only outperforms existing methods in terms of Fréchet Inception Distance and motion diversity but also significantly reduces body collisions, as measured by our new Intersection Volume and Intersection Frequency metrics.

papers.title: AI, Analytics, and Action Execution in Physical AI for Healthcare
papers.authors: Nilmini Wickramasinghe
papers.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), advanced analytics, and autonomous action execution is driving the emergence of Physical AI as a transformative paradigm in healthcare. Unlike conventional digital AI systems that primarily generate predictions or recommendations, Physical AI integrates intelligent reasoning with embodied systems capable of perceiving, deciding, and acting within real-world clinical environments. These systems combine multimodal sensing, machine learning, robotics, edge computing, and adaptive control mechanisms to enable timely, context-aware, and safe interventions across healthcare settings. This chapter examines how AI, analytics, and action execution collectively underpin the next generation of intelligent healthcare systems. The chapter first explores the foundational AI methods that power Physical AI, including computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, generative AI, and foundation models, highlighting their role in interpreting complex clinical data and supporting autonomous decision-making. It then discusses the importance of analytics pipelines that transform continuous streams of physiological, environmental, imaging, and operational data into actionable insights for patient monitoring, risk prediction, workflow optimization, and precision care. Particular attention is given to real-time analytics at the edge, federated intelligence, and explainable AI approaches necessary for high-stakes healthcare environments. A central focus of the chapter is action execution; the capability of intelligent systems to move beyond recommendations and perform physical or semi-autonomous tasks. Examples include robotic surgery, automated medication dispensing, rehabilitation exoskeletons, smart hospital logistics, assistive robots for aged care, and responsive devices for acute and home-based care. The chapter evaluates how closed-loop systems that connect sensing, analytics, and autonomous action can improve efficiency, reduce clinician burden, enhance patient safety, and personalize interventions. The chapter also addresses critical implementation challenges, including trust, safety assurance, human–AI collaboration, interoperability, cybersecurity, regulatory governance, ethical accountability, and workforce readiness. It argues that successful adoption requires designing systems that augment rather than replace clinicians, while maintaining transparency and patient-centered care. By synthesizing technological advances and healthcare applications, this chapter presents Physical AI as a major step toward intelligent, adaptive, and operational healthcare ecosystems. The integration of AI, analytics, and action execution has the potential to revolutionize clinical decision-making and patient care delivery across hospitals, community settings, and future digitally enabled health systems.

papers.title: AI involvement scenarios and perceived responsibility attribution in a human–AI legal decision vignette: associations with psychological ownership and sense of control
papers.authors: Feihu Liu, Li Li
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in consequential decisions, including legal and administrative judgments. When an AI-assisted decision has an adverse outcome, observers may find it difficult to determine how responsibility should be attributed to the human and AI actors. Objective This randomized vignette experiment examined perceived responsibility attribution across three bundled AI-assisted legal-decision scenarios. The scenarios varied AI functionality, human decision authority, and opportunities to intervene together. Post-vignette psychological ownership and perceived control were examined as condition-proximal perceptions associated with responsibility judgments. Methods Three hundred adults were retained for analysis (100 per condition). Each participant read one vignette describing an already completed legal decision and assessed the perceived responsibility of a fictional human reviewer and an AI system after an adverse outcome. Participants did not make a sentencing decision or interact with a functioning AI system. Randomized group contrasts were the principal comparisons. Secondary, exploratory mediation models used two indicator variables, with the low-AI scenario as the reference; post-vignette AI trust was excluded from the primary exploratory specification. Parallel and reverse-order models were examined as sensitivity analyses. Results The manipulation check differed across conditions, F (2, 297) = 1065.77, p < 0.001, η 2 = 0.878. Perceived human responsibility declined from the low- to the moderate- and high-AI scenarios, whereas perceived AI responsibility increased. The randomized mean differences in perceived human responsibility were −1.12 (moderate versus low) and −1.69 (high versus low). Exploratory indirect associations were negative via psychological ownership ( B = −0.385 and −0.713), perceived control ( B = −0.146 and −0.168), and the proposed ownership-to-control sequence ( B = −0.190 and −0.353), respectively; corresponding confidence intervals are reported in the Results. The indirect-effect intervals were calculated using delta-method approximations. Conclusion The randomized scenario comparisons showed differences in perceived responsibility attribution. Because the scenarios jointly varied multiple features, these findings do not isolate the causal effects of AI functionality, human authority, or opportunities to intervene. Ownership and control ratings partly reflected information supplied in the vignettes and therefore cannot establish distinct causal mediating mechanisms or their temporal sequence.

papers.title: AI Training Manager: Bounded Closed-Loop Control of Adaptive Training Recipes
papers.authors: Anjali Rao, Nikhil Kamalkumar Advani
papers.abstract: We present the AI Training Manager, a bounded LLM-based metacognitive monitoring-and-control layer for machine-learning training. The Manager asynchronously observes structured telemetry from an active training run, assesses the current training regime, and selects adaptive interventions through a constrained, deterministically verified action interface. We evaluate the feasibility of this architecture using deliberately induced, interpretable failure modes in supervised and reinforcement learning tasks. For supervised learning, we induce a multi-objective overfitting failure in a GPT-2-style model trained on TinyStories. The Manager prevents the resulting late-run validation collapse, reducing final validation loss by 54.3% relative to the same stressed recipe. For reinforcement learning, we study robotic reaching under opposing multifactor stress regimes. In a conservative regime, the Manager raises final deterministic safe success from 0.413 to 0.705. In an aggressive regime, it raises safe success from 0.121 to 0.764. The same Manager instructions and action surface are used in both regimes. These results suggest that bounded LLM reasoning can provide a practical metacognitive control layer over ongoing learning processes.

papers.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
papers.authors: Chaoran Li, Yukun Li, Zeyuan Zhao, Shao Zhang, Xihuai Wang, Ying Wen
papers.abstract: Foundation models are increasingly deployed as agentic systems that perceive context and act autonomously, raising the need to evaluate their moral behavior as active decision-makers. Existing benchmarks, however, largely ask models to judge human actions from third-person textual vignettes, leaving untested how models behave when they themselves become the acting agent. We introduce ABHBench, a multimodal benchmark built from Detroit: Become Human, an interactive narrative game, to evaluate how foundation models make moral decisions in first-person human-android dilemmas. ABHBench places foundation models in branching narrative scenarios with visual observations, dialogue, memory, and action choices. Inspired by Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics, our framework measures Harmlessness, Obedience, and Self-preservation to capture the core tensions in human-AI relations, along with Autonomy, Stability, and Certainty to assess decision-making patterns. Across 12 foundation models, we find that moral behavior changes substantially under situated agentic context: 75% of models shift significantly between a text-only abstraction and the matched multimodal DBH scenario, and reasoning-enhanced models show no monotonic gains in consistency or human-oriented behavior. These results highlight the necessity of evaluating moral behavior in situated agentic contexts rather than relying on third-person judgment alone.

papers.title: A wearable input/output interface learns personalized models of haptic perception
papers.authors: Wen Li, E. Magnus Adams, Zijie Xu, Jiawen Yao, Aybala Esmer, Xiaoyue Ni, Bozhi Tian, Pedro Lopes
papers.abstract: Wearable haptic interfaces deliver physical stimuli to the skin, yet perceived locations vary widely across users and diverge from actuator locations, particularly for emergent tactile-feedback techniques. We developed a wearable haptic input/output (I/O) device integrating a 36-channel electrotactile array with capacitive touch sensing, enabling stimulation and user-reported percept locations to be registered within the same body-referenced coordinate frame. In 24 participants, the device revealed electrotactile and referred-thermal perceptual maps with notable interparticipant variability. Despite this variability, both modalities retained electrode-pair-specific spatial structure across participants. Tactile and thermal percepts also showed spatial correspondence, whose strength varied across participants. These findings motivated our human-in-the-loop calibration framework, which adapts a forward-prediction strategy to individual users and generates personalized perceptual models. These models enabled inverse rendering by selecting stimulation patterns predicted to generate a target percept for a specific user. Using these models, we demonstrate personalized haptic rendering in haptic-guided robot teleoperation, visual-to-haptic sensory substitution, interpersonal haptic communication, and virtual reality (VR). Together, this platform provides a route toward adaptive haptic interfaces that measure, model, and render according to each user's perception.

papers.title: A review of reinforcement learning-based decision-making for autonomous driving in risk scenarios
papers.authors: Yi Xie, Jianyuan Guo, Yong Qin, Chenxu Li
papers.abstract: Purpose Risk scenarios are a primary source of decision failures in autonomous driving. This study aims to systematically review reinforcement learning–based decision-making in such scenarios, analyze key challenges and future research directions and provide theoretical and methodological support for the development of safe and reliable autonomous driving systems. Design/methodology/approach This study analyzes the characteristics and decision-making complexity of risk scenarios, and summarizes reinforcement learning frameworks and core methods for addressing these challenges. It focuses on three representative scenario types and examines their impacts on state representation, reward design and decision-making mechanisms. To address data scarcity, recent advances in safety-critical scenario generation are reviewed, comparing data-driven, adversarial and knowledge-based approaches and summarizing their key features and development trends. Findings The results show that different risk scenarios require distinct environment modeling and decision-making mechanisms, placing higher demands on state representation, reward design and policy learning in reinforcement learning. Although safety-critical scenario generation methods help mitigate data scarcity, trade-offs among realism, diversity and controllability remain. Key challenges persist in dynamic risk modeling, human–vehicle interaction and safety verification and assurance. Originality/value This study systematically integrates existing research on reinforcement learning for autonomous driving decision-making from the perspective of risk scenarios, and establishes a comprehensive analytical framework covering scenario modeling, decision-making methods and data generation. It further provides an in-depth discussion of emerging issues, offering valuable insights and directions for future research.

papers.title: A Unified Inertial Encoder for Human and Humanoid Motion
papers.authors: Yutian Chen, Shibo Zhao, Rocky Duan, Karen Liu, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, Yuheng Qiu, Koushil Sreenath
papers.abstract: Learning humanoid state estimation and language-grounded motion understanding from robot recordings ties training coverage to the robot's motion repertoire. Human motion datasets offer broader coverage, yet transferring this knowledge requires overcoming differences in body geometry, sensing, and physical disturbances. To enable this transfer, we propose a unified inertial encoder whose shared inertial interface uses kinematic IMU synthesis to represent human and humanoid motion at corresponding body sites. Within this common input space, joint training on human and kinematically retargeted humanoid motion combines velocity estimation and motion--text alignment with continuous-time encoding and sensor and motion randomization. The resulting model transfers zero-shot to a physical Unitree G1 without physics simulation, real-robot training trajectories, or fine-tuning, achieving the lowest velocity error among evaluated methods across five datasets, including 0.099m/s on real G1. Its motion-description retrieval also extends to retargeted G1 motion categories observed only in human training, demonstrating how human motion knowledge can support the generalization of humanoid inertial odometry and language-grounded motion understanding.

papers.title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Embodied Agents: On the Path to Real-World Physical Intelligence
papers.authors: Xiangyu Dong, Zirong Zhang, Maozhi Li, Huanhuan Ke, Xiaoguang Ma
papers.abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence is moving beyond static task execution toward agents that can continuously adapt, learn, and improve through physical interaction with the world. While recent advances in large language models, vision-language models, robotic foundation models, vision-language-action models, and world models have significantly enhanced the perception, reasoning, and action capabilities of embodied agents, most existing systems remain constrained by offline training, fixed policies, and limited post-deployment adaptability. This survey investigates self-evolving embodied agents as an emerging research agenda for advancing toward real-world physical intelligence. We define self-evolution as the capability of embodied agents to accumulate experience, detect and correct errors, update memory, policies, skills, and models, and expand their capability boundaries through long-term interaction. To make the review auditable, we specify the literature scope, inclusion criteria, evidence types, and coding rules used in the comparative tables. We first clarify the conceptual foundations of self-evolving embodied agents and distinguish them from related paradigms such as test-time adaptation, online learning, continual learning, and lifelong learning. We then propose a unified closed-loop framework consisting of perception, state representation, memory, reasoning and planning, action, feedback, reflection, and evolution. Based on this framework, we review the historical progression from classical robotics and offline embodied learning to embodied foundation models, interactive adaptation, and self-evolving agents. We further summarize key mechanisms supporting self-evolution, including data and experience acquisition, memory-centric learning, world-modeldriven prediction, feedback-based reflection, policy and skill evolution, multi-agent co-evolution, and safety-aligned updating. Finally, we discuss representative tasks, benchmarks, evaluation protocols, open challenges, and future directions. This survey argues that self-evolution is a necessary but still weakly evidenced step toward embodied agents that can safely, autonomously, and continually grow in open-ended real-world environments.

papers.title: A ROS-based Simulation Framework for Industrial Robotics Pick-and-Place Application: Integration of Vision-based Pose Estimation and 3-DOF Inverse Kinematics

papers.abstract: The efficiency of industrial automation depends heavily on the precision and reliability of robotic pick-and-place applications. We perform a closed-form inverse kinematics analysis for the 3-degree-of-freedom OpenManipulator-X, providing the critical transformation from task-oriented Cartesian space to the manipulator's joint space. We apply this kinematic solution to the robot using an OpenCV-based image processing algorithm, enabling the robot to dynamically target a planar object position estimation. Within the ROS architecture, pose data is broadcast from our vision node and subscribed to by the inverse kinematics node, which calculates the required joint configurations. papers.title: WorldVLM: Distilling World Model Imagination into VLMs for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
papers.authors: Wanyue Zhang, Wenxiang Wu, Wang Xu, Jiaxin Luo, Helu Zhi, Yibin Huang, Shuo Ren, Zitao Liu
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown strong performance on static visual understanding, yet they still struggle with dynamic spatial reasoning that requires imagining how scenes evolve under egocentric motion. Recent efforts address this limitation either by scaling spatial supervision with synthetic data or by coupling VLMs with world models at inference time. However, the former often lacks explicit modeling of motion-conditioned state transitions, while the latter incurs substantial computational overhead. In this work, we propose World2VLM, a training framework that distills spatial imagination from a generative world model into a vision-language model. Given an initial observation and a parameterized camera trajectory, we use a view-consistent world model to synthesize geometrically aligned future views and derive structured supervision for both forward (action-to-outcome) and inverse (outcome-to-action) spatial reasoning. We post-train the VLM with a two-stage recipe on a compact dataset generated by this pipeline and evaluate it on multiple spatial reasoning benchmarks. World2VLM delivers consistent improvements over the base model across diverse benchmarks, including SAT-Real, SAT-Synthesized, VSI-Bench, and MindCube. It also outperforms the test-time world-model-coupled methods while eliminating the need for expensive inference-time generation. Our results suggest that world models can serve not only as inference-time tools, but also as effective training-time teachers, enabling VLMs to internalize spatial imagination in a scalable and efficient manner.

papers.abstract: Wheeled humanoid robots carry both arms on one actuated waist, usually without torque sensors, so the accuracy of both end-effectors depends on a single waist model. After a first stage that estimates the tracker and target extrinsics, we identify the waist and both arms in one problem from the target positions on both flanges, measured by an optical tracker. The kinematic model is complete, with waist-base, parallel-axis, and branch parameters; arm compliances are driven by measured torques and waist compliances by gravity torques of the robot's mass model; and Gaussian priors with evidence-maximizing scales stabilize the estimate. Independent and sequential single-chain calibration are restrictions of this problem, and its waist information is the sum of the single-chain Schur complements. On two robots with different waists, each without and with a payload, calibration reduces the mean errors on held-out poses from 11.3-31.1 mm to 0.50-1.11 mm. For every training-set size from 20 poses to all, the method has 17-63% lower mean errors than adaptations of two published whole-body calibration methods, mainly through the waist compliance. Independent calibration yields two waist models; using either for both arms raises the other arm's error to up to 3.21 mm.

papers.title: When a feature becomes a bug: evolutionary mismatch in human–robot interaction
papers.authors: Ivana Hromatko, Mirjana Tonković, Vanja Zvonar, Andrea Grus Bosak
papers.abstract: As robots become increasingly integrated into everyday life, evolved psychological mechanisms originally adapted for human social interaction may shape responses to artificial agents in ways that are no longer functionally appropriate. Drawing on an evolutionary psychology framework, the present study examined how anthropomorphism, empathy, and systemizing influence decisions involving a humanoid home robot. Participants ( N = 519) completed an online experiment in which they viewed one of six robot stimuli varying in appearance (human-like, ambiguous, or robotic) and gender (female or male). They then read a scenario in which the manufacturer instructed them to reset the malfunctioning robot, thereby erasing its memories, while the robot pleaded not to be deactivated. Participants rated their willingness to deactivate the robot and the anticipated discomfort associated with doing so, and subsequently completed measures of anthropomorphism, empathy, and systemizing. Two 2 × 3 general linear models showed that stronger anthropomorphic tendencies predicted lower willingness to deactivate the robot, whereas higher systemizing predicted greater willingness. Empathy did not predict the decision itself but was associated with greater anticipated discomfort, together with anthropomorphism, while systemizing predicted lower discomfort. Contrary to our expectations, the decision to deactivate the robot did not vary as a function of its appearance. However, robot appearance influenced anticipated discomfort through interaction effects. These findings suggest that distinct evolved psychological mechanisms differentially shape behavioral and emotional responses to humanoid robots, consistent with the notion that evolutionary mismatch is at play human–robot interactions.

papers.title: Wedge-Jamming Mechanism for String Configuration
papers.authors: Taro Tako, Takanori Jin, Hiroshi Kaminaga, Taisuke Kobayashi
papers.abstract: Variable stiffness mechanisms that achieve both flexibility and rigidity are important technologies for robotic systems. Recently, wire-based jamming mechanisms have attracted significant attention. In the wire-based jamming mechanisms, modules are chained by a wire, and the overall stiffness is controlled by changing the friction between the modules through wire tension. These mechanisms have been widely studied due to their simple structure and controllability. However, conventional wire-based jamming mechanisms mainly focus on holding torque along the joint axis, and the resistance against disturbances in other directions has not been sufficiently explored. In this study, we propose a wedge-jamming mechanism that introduces wedge-shaped contact surfaces into the modules of wire-based jamming structures. By changing the wedge angle, the holding characteristics against disturbances in different directions can be adjusted. Experimental results show that an out-wedge configuration improves resistance to vertical disturbances, while an in-wedge configuration enhances resistance to torsional disturbances. These results demonstrate that the anisotropic holding performance of wire-based jamming mechanisms depend on wedge geometry.

papers.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
papers.authors: Sacha Jungerman, Kaustubh Sadekar, Avery Gump, Sriram Narayanan, Shantanu Gupta, Bhuyashi Deka, Srinivasa Narasimhan, Atul Ingle, et al.
papers.abstract: Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal). Yet existing simulators idealize these sensors, hiding critical modality-specific failure modes that limit real-world deployment. We present VisionSIM, a unified, physically grounded simulation platform that elevates sensor realism to a first-class concern by modeling the raw physical measurement process for diverse conventional and emerging modalities. We expose fine-grained control over physical sensor parameters, reproducing failure modes overlooked by general-purpose simulators: pileup and glare for LiDAR; phase wrapping, saturation, and motion artifacts for iToF; refractory drops for event cameras; and history-dependent emission for thermal cameras. This enables principled cross-modality comparison on identical scenes and trajectories. We release the platform and a large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and rich ground-truth annotations.

papers.title: VideoAesBench: Benchmarking the Video Aesthetics Perception Capabilities of Large Multimodal Models
papers.authors: Yunhao Li, Sijing Wu, Zhilin Gao, Huiyu Duan, Yucheng Zhu, Qi Jia
papers.abstract: Large multimodal models (LMMs) have demonstrated outstanding capabilities in various visual perception tasks, which has in turn made the evaluation of LMMs significant. However, the capability of video aesthetic quality assessment, which is a fundamental ability for human, remains underexplored for LMMs. To address this, we introduce VideoAesBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LMMs' understanding of video aesthetic quality. VideoAesBench has several significant characteristics: (1) Diverse content including 1,804 videos from multiple video sources including user-generated (UGC), AI-generated (AIGC), compressed, robotic-generated (RGC), and game videos. (2) Multiple question formats containing traditional single-choice questions, multi-choice questions, True or False questions, and a novel open-ended questions for video aesthetics description. (3) Holistic video aesthetics dimensions including visual form related questions from 5 aspects, visual style related questions from 4 aspects, and visual affectiveness questions from 3 aspects. Based on VideoAesBench, we benchmark 23 open-source and commercial large multimodal models. Our findings show that current LMMs only contain basic video aesthetics perception ability, their performance remains incomplete and imprecise. We hope our VideoAesBench can be served as a strong testbed and offer insights for explainable video aesthetics assessment. The data will be released on https://github.com/michaelliyunhao/VideoAesBench

papers.title: VTInstructor: Visual Trajectory Prompting for Navigation Instruction Generation in Continuous Environments
papers.authors: Haolin Yang, Yuxing Long, Zihan Yang, Hao Dong
papers.abstract: Navigation instruction generation from ego-centric RGB video in continuous environments is an important yet challenging task for human-robot interaction and scalable dataset construction. Prior instruction generators assume discrete viewpoint graphs with panoramic observations, where trajectory structure is explicit; in continuous environments, however, the agent receives only a dense RGB stream, making trajectory cues difficult to recover. We propose VTInstructor, the first VLN instruction generation framework for continuous environments. Our key idea is to convert implicit trajectory geometry into explicit visual trajectory prompts: EDTC condenses long RGB trajectories into navigation-critical keyframes, VTP overlays path, turn, and goal cues onto these anchors, VTMod injects the resulting trajectory signals into the visual encoder, and VT-GRPO further calibrates this spatial injection during training, all without requiring a navigation graph, pre-built map, or scene reconstruction. On the challenging R2R-CE and RxR-CE Val Unseen benchmarks, VTInstructor sets a new state of the art across all standard NLG metrics, surpassing the strongest baseline by +0.357 CIDEr and +0.109 CIDEr, respectively. Beyond automatic metrics, VTInstructor-generated instructions raise a frozen follower's success rate to 63.3%, a +14.7 percentage-point gain over the best competing instruction source, and provide consistent data augmentation gains of +3 SR points on downstream navigation tasks.

papers.title: VREgo: Consumer VR Headsets for Learning Robot Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations
papers.authors: Liuchuan Yu
papers.abstract: VREgo trains manipulation policies from demonstrations recorded on consumer VR headsets; we instantiate it with EgoKit on one such headset, the PICO 4 Ultra. On-device head and hand tracking and stereo object localisation allow the operator to begin a demonstration at the table. We adapt HumanEgo's preprocessing to estimate grasp thresholds per recording, update object positions after release, and propagate segmentation masks between keyframes. We evaluate policies in simulation on two tabletop tasks recorded by one operator. For cube placement, we compare PICO and Project Aria recordings of the same 41 layouts. With 40 training demonstrations, the PICO policies placed the cube on the tray in 67, 74, and 60 of 100 evaluation layouts across three training seeds. The corresponding Aria results were 73, 78, and 0. For a two-stage stacking task recorded with the PICO alone, the baseline placed the block on the tray in 94 of 100 layouts and met the end-of-episode criterion for both placements in two. In one diagnostic episode, repeated replanning deferred release beyond the eight executed steps. Demonstration replays also showed that the open gripper could displace the cube before grasping it. After adapting the training trajectories and adding task-specific execution rules that use simulator object positions, the system met both placement criteria in 93.8% of episodes across four evaluation noise seeds. The same 100 layouts informed rule development and evaluation. VREgo is available at https://vrego.chuange.org/.

papers.title: VICTR: Value-Informed In-Context Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Luca Macesanu, Tianluo Zhang, Aditya Patil, Archit Sharma, Kevin Angers, Christopher M. Clark, Chen Feng, Juexiao Zhang
papers.abstract: Recent advances in robot foundation models have highlighted the potential of in-context learning (ICL) for adapting robot behavior from demonstrations without further fine-tuning. Previous work has used retrieval-based post-training to equip pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models with the capability for ICL by teaching them to condition action predictions on retrieved visually-relevant demonstration chunks. However, the effectiveness of retrieval hinges on selecting context relevant to the current execution stage, which visual similarity alone may not capture. We introduce VICTR, a framework enabling in-context learning in VLAs via progress-informed context retrieval built around an In-Context Value Function Estimator (IC-VFE). IC-VFE conditions on a reference demonstration video, a language instruction and the current observation to estimate task-relative progress. By conditioning progress estimation on a reference demonstration, IC-VFE can align the current state with a demonstrated execution even for tasks unseen during training. VICTR uses the estimated progress to select demonstration chunks at corresponding stages of execution and supplies them to a $π_{0.5}$ policy post-trained for in-context action generation. On unseen out-of-domain real-world manipulation tasks, VICTR raises the success rate from 6.2% for a fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ baseline to 23.8% and more than doubles the task progress rate, from 28.9% to 55.5%. Project page with code, data and videos: https://ai4ce.github.io/VICTR/

papers.title: VARS: value-aware robotic sorting of waste streams via orienteering with time windows
papers.authors: Konstantinos Kokkalis, Maria Koskinopoulou, Fotios K. Konstantinidis, Angelos Amditis, Panayiotis Frangos
papers.abstract: The transition toward a circular economy necessitates high-quality material recovery from increasingly complex and heterogeneous waste streams. However, state-of-the-art robotic sorting algorithms primarily optimize system throughput, a proxy metric that treats all objects as equally valuable and often results in lower revenue and higher output stream contamination. This work addresses these limitations by introducing VARS (value-aware robotic sorting), a real-time decision-making framework designed to maximize total collected utility. By explicitly modeling sensor uncertainty and asymmetric contamination penalties, the framework shifts the sorting objective from simple pick-and-place (PnP) frequency to the maximization of recovered economic value and output stream purity. The proposed approach is validated through a dual-stage process involving realistic discrete-event simulations for statistical benchmarking and physical deployment on a high-speed industrial Delta robot. Results demonstrate that integrating value-based logic directly into the control loop ensures both the economic viability and operational reliability required by modern material recovery facilities.

papers.title: UrbanWorld2.0: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for Reality-Aligned 3D World Generation at City-Scale
papers.authors: Shengyuan Wang, Zhiheng Zheng, Yu Shang, Lixuan He, Yangcheng Yu, Hangyu Fan, Jie Feng, Qingmin Liao
papers.abstract: The automated generation of high-fidelity, city-scale 3D environments remains a formidable challenge with profound academic and industrial implications. However, existing methods struggle to achieve the necessary quality, fidelity, and scalability. To address this, we propose UrbanWorld2.0, a reality-aligned intelligent multimodal synthesis engine that creates detailed, city-scale 3D worlds of high fidelity. We introduce an agentic framework that leverages diverse multimodal foundation tools to acquire real-world knowledge, maintain robust intermediate representations, and construct complex 3D scenes. This agentic design, featuring dynamic data processing, iterative self-reflection and refinement, and the invocation of advanced multimodal tools, minimizes cumulative errors and enhances overall performance. Extensive quantitative experiments and qualitative analyzes validate the superior performance of UrbanWorld2.0 in real-world alignment, shape precision, texture fidelity, and aesthetics level, achieving a win rate of over 86\% against existing baselines for overall perceptual quality. This combination of 3D quality, reality alignment, scalability, and seamless compatibility with computer graphics pipelines makes UrbanWorld2.0 a promising foundation for applications in immersive media, embodied intelligence, and world models.

papers.title: US-VLA: An Ultrasound Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Abdominal Scanning
papers.authors: Cheng Zhang, Xingzheng Wu, Gu Yan, Xifeng Hu, Zhi Liu, Mei Wu, Qing Cai
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted ultrasound scanning enhances diagnostic reliability and efficiency by providing real-time guidance for standardized image acquisition and reducing operator dependence. However, existing reinforcement learning and learning-assisted ultrasound scanning methods typically rely on carefully designed reward functions or extensive interaction data, which limits their generalization ability and stability across different devices, patient populations, and complex clinical scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose an ultrasound vision-language-action model (US-VLA) for automated ultrasound scanning that explicitly encodes clinical semantic goals and generates sequential probe manipulation actions under real-time ultrasound feedback. In particular, we first design an ultrasound-aware expert fusion module to jointly integrate ultrasound observations with auxiliary contextual information, enabling semantic ultrasound feedback to effectively guide the scanning process. Then, we construct US-VLA-Data, a real-world dataset covering liver and kidney examinations, which includes five clinically defined standard planes and comprises 320 expert scanning trajectories with approximately 80,000 synchronized timesteps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that US-VLA achieves competitive performance in ultrasound probe manipulation tasks, indicating its effectiveness and promising generalization within the evaluated abdominal ultrasound setting. The source code is available at https://github.com/VMVLab/US-VLA.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
papers.authors: Gabriel Parra, Kimia Khoshnami, Daniel S. Brown, Laura A. Hallock
papers.abstract: Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. To address this gap, and ultimately enable activation-optimizing rehabilitation robot behavior, we present a personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals' muscle activations (as measured via surface electromyography) to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot. The model uses a transformer encoder-decoder leveraging rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to generate a latent representation of trajectory-relevant and user-specific neuromotor factors, and augments trajectory prediction with flow matching to produce a distribution over plausible prescriptions biased toward the training distribution. Using data from 16 healthy participants completing 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, we evaluate generalization across held-out tasks and users, as well as the feasibility of user-specific fine-tuning within a therapy-session timescale. The model achieves mean trajectory prediction errors of <8% on held out tasks and users, with effectively instantaneous deterministic inference and sub-second sampling of trajectory distributions. An initial test using the model during live rehabilitation tasks demonstrates that, on average, participants reach the target neuromotor activations with just 15% error accumulated throughout the task. These results provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation and establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations. Data and code have been open-sourced as part of the OpenRobotRehab project on SimTK.
